MORGAN STANLEY INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE – Placements (July, 2019) 
Morgan Stanley had criteria of CPI 8.0 or above, to be eligible for the aptitude test. Around 103 were 
eligible. 
APTITUDE TEST: 
• 
Section 1: 
There were 7 debugging questions. Time limit of 20 minutes. 
6 were easy and one was tricky. 
 
• 
Section 2: 
There were 10 MCQs based on aptitude, pie charts, logical reasoning. Time limit of 20 
minutes. 
 
• 
Section 3: 
There were 3 coding questions. Time limit of 60 minutes. 
 
1. Given an array of integers of size n and some integer k where 0 <= k < n.  
You have to sort first k elements in ascending order and rest of the elements in descending 
order. 
 
2. One user can buy products having product names from a-z. Name of products is only one 
character long. Now given 2 orders of a user and an integer k, you have to output all ways in 
which user can buy k elements from common products of given 2 orders. 
In this question, if uppercase letter is present, you have to make it lower case 
Sample case: - CtERYuq 
 
           tHUQZXc 
 
           3 
Output: ctu ctq cuq tuq 
 
3. Graph question: Given some undirected edges and some directed, you have to do dfs 
from some of those points and return max length. 
 
Problem statements of these problems were quite lengthy. Here I have mentioned the crux 
of the problems. Speed is the key here, though you should be able to select easy problems 
first so as to solve them before time runs out. For this try to practice solving problems in 
timed format. 
 
TECHNICAL INTERVIEW 1: 
Around 11 candidates were shortlisted for this round. Two interviewers per candidate. 
Duration: 100 minutes 
• 
Tell me about yourself 
• 
You have one search bar and two buttons of undo and redo. You can type anything in the 
search bar like backspace, Clt+Shift+a, etc. and every time a key is pressed a function of 
onKeyChange(String s) will get called.

Here, question was little vague. I had to enquire about what string is passed onto the 
function, how undo and redo will operate, is there a limit on redo operation. 
First, I didn’t have clear understanding of the given problem, I was considering that every 
time a key is pressed, we get the same character again. So, I proposed solution according to 
my understanding of the question. Midway on solution they corrected my assumption and 
made me start once again. They told that every time a key is pressed whole string gets 
passed on. Then it was not much of a problem. Two stacks did the trick. While explaining 
they were expecting pseudo code and also code to handle corner cases. 
 
• 
I was given a matrix having some elements and rest of elements having no value, a sparse 
matrix basically. They asked about ways to store this matrix 
I asked them if this problem is in database domain or data structures domain. They said data 
structures. So, I told them that I will have a hash map of pair<int, int> and value. Pair 
containing row and column as index. But then they countered me by calculating size of that 
data structure which by the way blew me off (something like see this is using 20% more 
space so why this structure and what if matrix is not sparse then it be like 70% and then 2D 
array is better than your structure). I was thinking that who thinks this much. (Just use Hash 
map :D). Then by having mercy on me they asked me about how will you output data of 
some specific column. So, I said give me number of rows, I will iterate it for that column. So, 
complexity will be O(n). Now they said what if you don’t know the number of rows. 
So, then I asked should I tell my database approach. They said yes. So, I told them that. 
 
• 
Now they moved on to OOPS concepts. Asked me to create immutable object. 
I asked them if I can explain it in Java. 
 
• 
Some questions (I don’t remember now) 
 
• 
They gave me a set of integers and asked to generate all power set of this given set.  
Asked me to write code for it. I gave them some non-trivial answer which was not optimal 
(in my opinion) but it worked. They had some difficulty understanding it. (P.S. I derived that 
solution using combinatorics then and there only) 
 
• 
Asked me if I have any question. I asked some 
 
TECHNICAL INTERVIEW 2: 
 Four candidates were shortlisted for this round 
Duration: 110 minutes 
• 
Tell me about yourself 
• 
Asked me to explain my internship project which I did in SRIB. 
Then they went on to ask, if you did such good project why didn’t you get the PPO. I said I 
want to work only for your company :D 
 
• 
Now, he asked me to design Facebook 
So, I first explained what features should our fictional Facebook have. He then deleted some 
features and added a few. (As it has a ton of features)

I then asked If I should design this in relational database or NoSQL, he said for now relational 
database, if time permits NoSQL. 
Then I enlisted all the entities and their attributes after that.  
Now when I was to add some feature, I was constantly updating entities. And their 
relationship between each other. He also asked to keep good names for entities. 
Entities were like User, Post, Comment, Friend, FriendRequest, Like, etc 
 
We discussed about how friend requests will work. I explained it using notifications and 
triggers where friendrequest entity will hold request and after acceptation or rejection, it 
will get added to friend entity 
 
Then he asked me to store all this data in memory like a cache, so which data structure will I 
use and write its code. 
 
We then discussed about how search will work. I then suggested trie approach and have 
mapping of userid to user class. Tries terminal node will have that set of userid. He then 
asked me what if I search by last name. Then I said we’ll also save that information in same 
trie. Now he asked what if the I search only first 3 characters, how will I get the desired 
result? I said then by searching for whole subtree, I will retrieve set of userids.  
Then he said you have designed much. Take this new page and implement whole trie 
without scratching any code. I did it. (Without scratching a word😉 ) 
 
• 
Asked me if I have any question. I asked some 
 
In this type of interview, if you are going on wrong track, they will give you hints. And you 
are then expected to follow them. You have to be confident while explaining what you will 
use and what you will not by having appropriate reasons. Mostly this type of system design 
question will only be asked in Morgan Stanley. 
 
HR INTERVIEW: 
Duration: 30 minutes 
• 
Tell about me about yourself 
• 
Explain everything on your resume 
Don’t explain it by looking at your resume. You should know what’s there and what’s not 
• 
How were your both interviews? 
• 
Where do you think you lacked? 
• 
What if one of the two interviewers think that you are not good at data structures, and 
assume that you are the other interviewer who think otherwise. What would you tell your 
co-interviewer? 
You have to sell yourself in this question 
• 
Consider a scenario you are working in a project where product is going to get launched on 
Saturday and you encountered a bug on Friday night, what will you do? What if that bug is 
not going to get noticed anytime soon? What if your team members are reluctant to work 
on weekend? What if your promotion is due on next week?

Just tell them you will try to resolve bug no matter what, no matter when even if it affects 
your prospects 
• 
Now consider the same scenario, but the project member is your childhood mate and you 
encountered the bug what will you do? 
• 
Then executive director came and asked some puzzles 
• 
3 litres jug and 5 litres jug, you have to make 4 litres of water using only 8 litres of water 
• 
He has a revolver, which has 6 bullet holes and 2 bullets in consecutive position. He shoots 
you, and you are saved. So, he has two options either roll the bullet barrel or shoot the next 
bullet. Which option would you go for so as to increase your chances of survival? 
Derive using probability 
• 
They were asking me question of 2 strings of 60 minutes required burning time each. I said I 
know it. Then they moved on to the next question 
• 
100 people are standing in a circle. 1st man kills 2nd and 3rd and passes sword to the 4th 
person. And this goes on. Who will be the last standing person? 
 
They just try to look to your approach and it doesn’t matter if you reach the solution or not. 
Just explain all your thinking process. 
 
At last 3 were selected. 
 
Have your basics clear about data structures, algorithms. Know how to tackle system design 
questions. Be polite and honest. All the best!! 
 
 
~ Jayant Rane
